title: gray_code_iter shared subset enumerator
description:
Implement the Gray-code subset enumerator that the Ryser permanent inner loop walks; shared by T7 (`permanent_ryser`) and T9 (`permanent_bipedal3`).

## Background

Ryser's permanent formula iterates over all $2^n - 1$ non-empty subsets of $[n]$. Walking subsets in Gray-code order means consecutive iterations differ by exactly one bit (one element added or removed), which lets the column-sum vector update in a single column add/sub instead of recomputing from scratch.

The enumerator yields `(flip_index: usize, parity: i8)` tuples where `flip_index` is the bit toggled at this step and `parity` is +1 (added) or -1 (removed). Both T7 (generic over `FiniteField`) and T9 (bipedal3 fast path) reuse this iterator; placing it in `gf2-algebra::permanent::gray` shares the implementation and the correctness tests.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::gray::gray_code_iter(n: usize) -> impl Iterator<Item = (usize, i8)>` exists.
- [ ] [hard] The iterator yields exactly $2^n - 1$ items for $n \in \{1, \ldots, 16\}$ and the cumulative XOR of the bit-vector indexed by `flip_index` traverses every non-empty subset of $[n]$ exactly once.
- [ ] [hard] Sum of `parity` values across the full iteration equals the running popcount of the current subset; verified via running-state assertion in tests.
- [ ] [hard] Tests cover $n \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16\}$ exhaustively.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes; total runtime < 1 s.
